{{short description|Canadian born experimental physicist (born 1972)}}
'''Oskar Painter''' is a [[Canadian]] born (1972) experimental [[physicist]] who works on [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] [[optics]], [[Nanomechanics|nanomechanical]] devices, and [[superconducting qubits]]. He is the John G. Braun Professor of Applied Physics and Professor of Physics at [[Caltech]]. Since 2019, he is also Head of Quantum Hardware at [[Amazon Web Services]] (AWS).

Painter received his PhD from [[Caltech]] in 2001 under the supervision of Prof. [[Axel Scherer]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Painter |first1=Oskar Jon |title=Optical nanocavities in two-dimensional photonic crystal planar waveguides |date=2001 |publisher=California Institute of Technology |url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/5155/|type=phd }}</ref>  After graduation, Painter helped found Xponent Photonics along with Pete Sercel and Caltech colleagues Kerry Vahala and Amnon Yariv.  Painter joined the Caltech faculty in 2002, as an assistant professor of Applied Physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oskar J. Painter |url=https://aph.caltech.edu/people/opainter |website=Caltech Applied Physics |access-date=24 February 2020}}</ref> In 2012, he became Director at the [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]] and was awarded a [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship|Humboldt Professorship]] in 2013. In 2014, he returned to Caltech.  Painter has also served as the co-director of the [[Fred Kavli#Nanoscience|Kavli Nanoscience Institute]]<ref>{{cite web |title=5 Questions about Quantum Engineering with Oskar Painter |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D6shjbL4aUw |website=YouTube | date=7 December 2017 |access-date=24 February 2020}}</ref> and co-PI of the Institute of Quantum Information and Matter during his time at Caltech.

Painter's research has covered many topics, including photonic crystals and silicon photonics, to solid-state cavity quantum electrodynamics and quantum [[optomechanics]]. More recently, he has shifted his research towards superconducting quantum circuits, with a particular emphasis on hybrid circuit architectures involving the integration of optical and nanomechanical devices.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Keller |first1=Andrew J. |last2=Dieterle |first2=Paul B. |last3=Fang |first3=Michael |last4=Berger |first4=Brett |last5=Fink |first5=Johannes M. |last6=Painter |first6=Oskar |title=Al transmon qubits on silicon-on-insulator for quantum device integration |journal=Applied Physics Letters |date=24 July 2017 |volume=111 |issue=4 |pages=042603 |doi=10.1063/1.4994661|arxiv=1703.10195 |bibcode=2017ApPhL.111d2603K |s2cid=19540567 }}</ref>
